title: Fail closed or isolate merge gates when the reused-worktree lock is unavailable
description:
## Finding

The merge queue's default warm-gate path reuses one stable worktree per repository, but its cross-process serialization is both Unix-only and best-effort. On Windows `gate_lock()` always returns `None`; on Unix any directory/open/lock failure also returns `None`. `gate_tip()` then continues against the shared worktree rather than refusing the gate or falling back to a unique worktree.

## Evidence

* `crates/thegn-host/src/integrate.rs:655-688`: Unix `gate_lock()` discards `create_dir_all`, open, and lock errors through best-effort `Option` handling.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/integrate.rs:689-692`: non-Unix `gate_lock()` is unconditionally `None`.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/integrate.rs:735-755`: `gate_reuse_worktree` selects one stable per-repo `wt` path; the configuration default is `true` (`crates/thegn-core/src/config.rs:938`).
* `crates/thegn-host/src/integrate.rs:767`: failure to acquire serialization is ignored and gate preparation proceeds.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/integrate.rs:769-803`: concurrent callers can checkout/recreate that same path at different OIDs before executing their gates.

A CLI `merge drain`/`land` and a compositor/autopilot drain are separate processes, so loop-local serialization is insufficient. Under this interleaving, one invocation can report a green verdict for the other invocation's checkout and then advance a ref whose exact folded tip was never tested.

## Constraints

* Preserve the warm `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` optimization where safe.
* Do not serialize unrelated repositories.
* Lock acquisition/preparation failures are infrastructure failures, never branch gate failures and never fixing-agent input.
* Support every platform on which the local merge queue is exposed; do not silently weaken correctness on Windows.
* Avoid stale locks after process death.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Reused gate worktrees have a real cross-process exclusion mechanism on all supported platforms, or unsupported/unavailable locking automatically uses a unique throwaway worktree.
2. Lock creation/acquisition errors cannot continue into the shared reused worktree.
3. The lock covers the full prepare -> optional setup -> gate -> cleanup interval.
4. Two concurrent gate processes for the same repo/OIDs cannot mutate the same worktree concurrently or misattribute a verdict.
5. Concurrent gates for different repos remain independent.
6. Lock/setup failures surface as `GateVerdict::Error` (or equivalent infrastructure failure), never `Failed`.

## Verification

* Add a deterministic concurrency test using two processes or an injectable barrier around preparation/gate execution, asserting each verdict observes its requested OID.
* Add an acquisition-failure test proving the shared worktree is not touched.
* Exercise the non-Unix implementation in Windows CI (or a platform abstraction unit test compiled on Windows).
* Run the merge/integrate focused suite and `just quick`.

## Additional lock-identity evidence

The reused gate lock key is also derived from the raw caller path through `DefaultHasher` (`integrate.rs:653-670`). Equivalent symlink, relative, case-folded, or otherwise aliased paths to one repository can select different worktree/lock paths and run concurrently. The sidecar is opened by pathname with ordinary `OpenOptions`, without no-follow, owner/type/link-count verification, or a canonical repository-authority binding.

The fix must key the lock and gate root from a pinned canonical repository identity, open/create the sidecar through a private no-follow directory, and make lock acquisition failure a typed refusal or isolated unique-worktree fallback.
